Method: Optimal edge-fluctuation scales for arbitrary random-matrix polynomials structural calculation Result: The nondegeneracy qualifier is necessary even for a one-variable quadratic polynomial. For a standard GUE matrix G_N let P(x)=20-(x-2)^2. With probability tending to1 its spectrum lies in a fixed neighborhood of[-2,2] where P is positive. Then norm(P(G_N))=20-min_i(lambda_i-2)^2. Since the largest GUE eigenvalue is2+O_p(N^-2/3), one has0<=20-norm(P(G_N))<=O_p(N^-4/3). Check: The upper bound uses the largest eigenvalue as one candidate in the minimum. Spectral mapping and positivity give the norm identity. Consequently N^(2/3)*(norm(P(G_N))-20) tends to0, rather than a nondegenerate Tracy-Widom variable. Obstruction: The example is deliberately degenerate and does not contradict the stated research direction. A correct general theorem must identify regularity of the polynomial edge before asserting the universal scale.

entries.title: Attempt on Joint strong convergence for permutation and deterministic matrices
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Joint strong convergence for permutation and deterministic matrices structural calculation Result: Naively compressing arbitrary deterministic matrices creates persistent defects. Let e be the normalized all-ones vector, P=I-ee*, and B a balanced diagonal matrix with entries plus/minus1. B strongly converges to the symmetric Bernoulli law. But on e-perp, PBP has the zero eigenvector Be, while all its other eigenvalues are plus/minus1. Thus norm(I_(e-perp)-(PBP)^2)=1, whereas the corresponding Bernoulli-limit polynomial is zero. Check: Because B^2=I and e*Be=0, PBP(Be)=PB(e)=Pe=0. More generally (PBP)^2-PB^2P=-PBee*BP, whose norm here is1. Its normalized trace tends to0 but its operator norm does not. Obstruction: This refutes the naive unchanged-deterministic-limit formulation after compression, not every possible counterpart requested by the survey. Appropriate invariant subspaces or additional deterministic hypotheses remain to be formulated and proved.

entries.title: Attempt on Brown-measure convergence from general strong convergence
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Brown-measure convergence from general strong convergence structural calculation Result: Complete candidate counterexample: rational clock/shift unitary pairs U_j,V_j approach an irrational rotation pair u,v strongly, while U_j^q=I and V_j^q=-I force det(zI-U_j-V_j)=z^q. Hence every finite sum is nilpotent with empirical measure delta_0. The established Brown measure of u+v is Haar measure on the unit circle. Simultaneous Haar conjugation makes the finite family random without changing any of these statements. Check: The strong-convergence proof maps the simple irrational rotation algebra into the product of matrix algebras modulo norm-null sequences; injectivity gives every subsequential limsup polynomial norm and therefore the full limit. Normalized word traces are checked directly. The determinant calculation independently checks nilpotency. Full proof and all source dependencies are in the proof packet. Obstruction: No gap presently identified in the literal-general-scope construction, but there is no independent review and no novelty claim. It does not resolve independent Ginibre polynomials with adjoints; the June2026 holomorphic-Ginibre theorem is compatible with this example.
assumptions: Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0189-brown-measure-convergence-from-general-strong-convergence

entries.title: Attempt on Intrinsic freeness for non-Hermitian eigenvalues
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Intrinsic freeness for non-Hermitian eigenvalues structural calculation Result: Hermitization exposes a missing hypothesis. Weak singular-value convergence and bounded largest singular value do not control the logarithmic potential: nu_N=(1-1/N)*delta_1+(1/N)*delta_(exp(-N)) converges weakly to delta_1 and has bounded support, but integral log(s) dnu_N=-1 rather than0. Thus a comparison based only on bounded polynomial spectral statistics cannot justify passage through the logarithm. Check: All positive moments converge to1, while the single tiny singular value contributes(1/N)*(-N)=-1. Uniform integrability of the negative logarithm would remove this particular obstruction. Obstruction: The scalar example is an obstruction to a proof step, not itself a counterexample to empirical eigenvalue convergence. Quantitative least-singular-value control adapted to intrinsic covariance models is still missing.

entries.title: Attempt on Least singular values at the polynomial constant term
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Least singular values at the polynomial constant term structural calculation Result: For a monomial P=X_(i1)...X_(id), the missing shift is0 and the estimate reduces to the individual matrices. Since smin(P)>=product_k smin(X_(ik)), the event smin(P)<=epsilon implies at least one factor has smin<=epsilon^(1/d). The standard complex-Ginibre bound then gives P(smin(P)<=epsilon)<=C*d*N^2*epsilon^(2/d). Repeated factors require no independence in this union bound. Check: For normalized complex Ginibre, N*smin has the usual bounded quadratic lower tail. Multiply the deterministic singular-value inequalities successively, and apply the union bound over the d factor positions. Obstruction: Sums of monomials can cancel, so this argument gives no least-singular-value estimate for an arbitrary noncommutative polynomial at its constant term.

entries.title: Attempt on Brown-measure universality beyond complex entry densities
entries.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Brown-measure universality beyond complex entry densities structural calculation Result: Every one-matrix holomorphic polynomial is already reducible to the circular law. If X_N has a circular-law limit and P is a fixed complex polynomial, spectral mapping gives mu_(P(X_N))=P_pushforward(mu_(X_N)) exactly, including algebraic multiplicities. The continuous mapping theorem therefore yields the pushforward of the circular law. The Brown measure of P(c) is the same pushforward, by factorizing P(z)-lambda and using multiplicativity of the Fuglede-Kadison determinant. Check: For each test function h bounded and continuous, h composed with P is bounded and continuous, so weak convergence passes through P. At the logarithmic-potential level, P(c)-lambda factors into commuting(c-root_j) terms, and determinant multiplicativity gives the same transformed Brown measure. Existing real-Gaussian and Bernoulli circular laws supply the initial one-matrix convergence. Obstruction: For several noncommuting input matrices there is no joint eigenvalue spectral mapping. Arithmetic and structural dependence in least-singular-value estimates remain unresolved here.
assumptions: Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0192-brown-measure-universality-beyond-complex-entry-densities
